v.q: A service has low CPU but every request hangs. What is the best first step?
o: Take three thread dumps about ten seconds apart and compare them
Take a heap dump and open it in Eclipse MAT
Raise -Xmx and restart the service
Enable Native Memory Tracking on the next deploy
v.w: Low CPU with hung requests means threads are waiting. Dumps taken over time show what they wait for. A heap dump shows memory, not waiting.

v.q: Which symptom is NOT a sign that threads are waiting instead of working?
o: One core stays at 100% CPU
CPU is low while requests hang
Threads sit in the same place in several dumps
A thread dump reports a Java-level deadlock
v.w: A busy core means a thread is running something hot, which is the high-CPU case. Waiting shows as low CPU and the same stack in every dump.

v.q: In a thread dump, which value lets you match a thread to the id shown by top -H?
o: nid, the operating-system thread id in hexadecimal
tid, the Java thread id in decimal
prio, the thread priority number
The name of the thread pool
v.w: top shows decimal ids, and the dump prints nid in hexadecimal, so convert with printf %x before searching.

v.q: Thread 4377 uses 97% CPU in top -H. Which value do you search for in the thread dump?
o: nid=0x1119
prio=4377
pid=0x1119
v.w: The dump prints the native thread id in hexadecimal. 4377 in decimal is 0x1119, so search for nid=0x1119.

v.q: After every full GC the heap is a little fuller than after the last one. What does this suggest?
o: A memory leak, so take a heap dump and look at the dominator tree
The young generation is too small for the allocation rate
A deadlock between two threads holding locks
The JIT compiler has not finished warming up
v.w: A rising heap after full GC means objects are still reachable but unused. High peaks with a flat floor point at sizing or allocation instead.

v.q: Which observation does NOT point at a memory leak?
o: The heap is high before a GC but falls back to the same floor
The heap after each full GC is higher than after the last one
Old generation stays full after full GC
Full GC runs often and frees almost nothing
v.w: A flat floor after GC means the garbage is collected. That is sizing or allocation, not a leak.

v.q: What does retained heap tell you about an object in a heap dump?
o: The memory that would be freed if that object were removed
The memory taken by the object's own fields only
The number of references that point to the object
The memory the object used before the last GC
v.w: Retained heap includes everything kept alive only by the object. Shallow heap is just the object itself. The dominator tree sorts by retained heap.

v.q: In a heap dump, what is the shallow heap of an object?
o: The memory of the object itself, without what it references
The memory freed if the object were removed
The memory of the object and every object it references
The memory the object had before the last GC
v.w: Shallow heap is only the object. Retained heap adds everything that would become unreachable without it.

v.q: A container is OOMKilled with exit code 137, but the Java heap is only 60% full. What is the likely reason?
o: Off-heap memory (threads, Metaspace, buffers) pushed the process over the limit
The garbage collector failed to run before the limit was reached
The JVM threw OutOfMemoryError and the heap dump was then lost
The heap dump flag was missing from the startup command line
v.w: The kernel limits the whole process, and kills it with SIGKILL, so there is no Java exception. Native Memory Tracking shows which area grew.

v.q: Which tool shows how much of a container's memory is used by Metaspace, thread stacks and buffers?
o: Native Memory Tracking
A heap dump in Eclipse MAT
The GC log alone
A thread dump
v.w: A heap dump and the GC log describe only the heap. NMT breaks the whole process down by area.

v.q: Which message means the JVM could not create another thread?
o: OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread
OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace
OutOfMemoryError: Direct buffer memory
v.w: The text after the colon names the exhausted area. A thread request refused by the operating system gives the native thread message.

v.q: Which message means the JVM ran out of space for class metadata?
o: OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace
OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
OutOfMemoryError: unable to create native thread
OutOfMemoryError: GC overhead limit exceeded
v.w: The text after the colon names the exhausted area. Metaspace holds class metadata and fills up with class-loader leaks.

v.q: Why is Java Flight Recorder considered safe to run in production?
o: It samples data the JVM already has, so the overhead is about one to two percent
It only runs while the service is idle at night
It records every method call with full arguments
It stops all threads while it writes the recording
v.w: JFR records sampled events instead of instrumenting each call. It can run continuously or start on demand with jcmd JFR.start.

v.q: Which statement about Java Flight Recorder is NOT true?
o: It records every method call with its arguments
It can start on demand with jcmd JFR.start
Its overhead is typically one or two percent
It records sampled events
v.w: JFR samples events instead of instrumenting every call, which is why it is safe in production.

v.q: In a flame graph, what does the width of a box mean?
o: The share of samples in which that method was on the stack
The time order in which the method ran
The number of threads that called the method
The memory the method allocated
v.w: Wide boxes are where time goes. The horizontal order has no meaning, so read from a wide box down to its callers.

v.q: In a flame graph, which box is the best place to start looking for slow code?
o: The widest box near the top of a stack
The leftmost box
The tallest stack
The box with the shortest method name
v.w: Width is the share of samples, so wide boxes are where time goes. The left-to-right order carries no meaning.
